items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Free for thirty days. Just enter your card. But why would they need your card for something free?
Narrator
Because the business isn't the trial. It's the day you forget.
Narrator
The trial ends, the card is charged, and it renews automatically, every month.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Cancel anytime, darling. If you can find the button.
Narrator
The F T C accused Amazon of signing people up for Prime without clear consent, and making it hard to cancel.
Narrator
Inside Amazon, the cancel process had a nickname: "Iliad" — after the famously long Greek epic.
Narrator
Amazon denied wrongdoing, but in twenty twenty-five it paid two point five billion dollars to settle, one point five billion of it in refunds.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the trial is free. Forgetting is what you pay for.
Narrator
The fix: set a reminder the day you sign up, and check your statement for charges you don't recognise.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched] Wait, what am I still paying for?
Narrator
Comment: which subscription did you forget to cancel?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
